messages:
yuki: Heads up — during the Calyx v1 int8 onboarding smoke we noticed a reproducible token-offset drift for mixed Chinese + Arabic inputs. Quick eval shows BLEU ~4 pts down on our zh->ar set. Anyone seen mixed-script offset issues after quantization?

eval-bot: automated eval summary for calyx-v1-int8 on nightly 2026-03-19: BLEU: 24.1 (baseline float16: 28.3), chrF: 0.482 -> 0.444, token_offset_mismatch: 132/1000 sampled lines. Example mismatch count concentrated on mixed zh + rtl substrings.

chen: can you paste a minimal repro pair and the tokenization/offsets? is this only on int8 or also on q4/q5 experiments?

yuki: minimal repro below (copied actual line from sample set):
source: 我们的文档里写了测试。 السلام عليكم
expected detokenized spans -> Arabic segment start at byte 16
calyx-v1-fp16 offsets: [0, 6, 9, 11, 14, 16, 28] (matches expected)
calyx-v1-int8 offsets:  [0, 6, 9, 11, 14, 15, 27] (Arabic segment start shifted -1)
so the Arabic token start moves left by one byte/token in many mixed lines.

ada: interesting. first thought: tokenizer pretokenization vs normalization change + quantized model returning slightly different tokenization decisions (if we use subword scoring for greedy merges). but offset shifts usually come from pretokenizer or offset mapping bug in the tokenizer lib. can you run tokenizer.encode_plus with return_offsets_mapping on both model tokenizers (the shipped tokenizer artifact for fp16 vs int8) and diff the mappings?

chen: run this quick check:
```
python tools/token_offset_check.py \
  --tokenizer artifacts/calyx-v1/tokenizer.json \
  --samples samples/zh_ar_mixed.txt \
  --out out/offsets_int8.csv
```
Make sure you compare the tokenizer artifact used for the int8 build vs the fp16 build.

yuki: ran that; attaching the short table (pasted):
line 12: fp16_offsets: [(0,1),(1,3),(3,6),(6,9),(9,12),(12,28)]
line 12: int8_offsets: [(0,1),(1,3),(3,6),(6,9),(9,11),(11,27)]
So it's the mapping stage, not downstream alignment. Also saw zwnj/zwj presence in a few lines triggering different cluster merges.

sven: we've seen similar before when normalization changed (NFC vs NFKC) and a zero-width joiner got folded differently, which shifts subsequent offsets. confirm the normalization pipeline at tokenization entry. which version of tokenizers runtime is being bundled into the int8 build? could be an older rust-tokenizers binary.

ada: also check if we accidentally switched to 'use_bytes' fallback for unknown bytes in the quant path (we do a tiny fallback in some kernel paths which can change pretokenization). grep for 'use_bytes' in the int8 packaging script.

maria: from rollout perspective — calyx-v1-int8 is currently canary at 1% for dedicated and 0.5% for hosted. if this is affecting zh-ar mixes we should pause canary for locales flagged by the eval (zh->ar, ar->zh). what do you recommend?

yuki: propose PAUSE canary for multilingual locales touching CJK or RTL until we confirm root cause. I'll open a rollback flag to q4f16 for the canary groups.

ops-bot: deploy: canary config updated by yuki — paused mixed-locale traffic for calyx-v1-int8 canary at 2026-03-19T14:12Z.

chen: I'll bisect the packaging changes between the last good fp16 artifact and the int8 artifact. PRs to check: quant-packaging#421, tokenizer-upgrade#398, rust-tokenizers#210. I'll run a narrow bisect focusing on tokenizers/runtime changes.

sven: also run a unit that injects zero-width joiner and narrow no-break spaces into our samples and assert offsets are stable before metric computation. if flaky, add a guard in the eval pipeline to normalize to NFC and re-run baseline.

yuki: action items: (1) chen bisect packaging + report by EOD, (2) ada to run tokenizer.encode_plus diffs and confirm normalization mode, (3) sven to add offset-stability check in eval harness, (4) maria keep canary paused for mixed locales until we have a fix/qa signoff.

maria: thanks — please ping me once the bisect points to a change, we'll coordinate rollback or patch release. :+1:

yuki: will do. adding labels: #onboard #quantization #tokenization #multilingual
